<FeatureHeader id="fun_death" />

## What it does

In v1, `/death` (also `/morte`, `/muerte`) posts a random image or gif —
someone's tag or a random "cause of death" — captioned with a randomised
"is dead!"-style line and a silly reason pulled from an 81-line pool. It
can target the caller, a tagged name, or whoever they replied to.

## Why this one is blocked, not just unstarted

v1's image pool is not a file checked into its repository — it is a live
listing of a private Google Cloud Storage bucket
(`bloblist_death = list(storage_bucket.list_blobs(prefix="Death"))`,
`Miscellaneous.py:17`), fetched fresh at process start and read with
15-minute signed URLs. Nothing in `../COOKIEBOT-Telegram-Group-Bot`'s
checked-in static tree carries those files, and nothing in this repository
or environment has a credential for that bucket. `fun_complaint` and
`fun_meme`'s templates are the counter-example: those *are* checked into
v1's static tree, which is why they could be vendored byte-identical the way
`cb_core/asset_data/complaint/` already is.

The everything-else of this feature — the target resolution, the caption
assembly, the gate, the locale strings (the `death.txt` reason pool and the
`death` catalog block are both already ported byte-identical) — is fully
specified and ready to build. The full behaviour contract and evidence for
the blocker live in
[`.specs/features/fun_death/spec.md`](https://github.com/Cookiebot-Team/cookiebot-telegram-bot/blob/main/.specs/features/fun_death/spec.md);
a design and task breakdown are written ahead of time in the same directory
so the port is mechanical the moment someone exports the bucket's `Death/`
prefix.
